describe_model.title: Describe Model
describe_model.description: Return the complete schema of all entities, attributes, relationships, and enum cases. Call this before any other tool — attribute names are system-specific and cannot be guessed (e.g. isEnabled, not isActive).

fetch.title: Fetch
fetch.description: Fetch entity rows with optional filtering, sorting and pagination. Call once per query — trust the result even if count is 0; do not retry with rephrased predicates.

count.title: Count
count.description: Count entities matching an optional predicate.

aggregate.title: Aggregate
aggregate.description: Compute aggregate values for an entity.

group_by.title: Group By
group_by.description: Group rows and compute aggregates. Call once per query — if rowCount is 0, data is absent; do not retry with different arguments or aliases.

create.title: Create
create.description: Create one entity row, including any related objects nested under `values` (attributes, to-one and to-many relationships, and deeper graphs) in a single call. Use this whenever a row has relationships or nested objects — even when creating several related rows at once. Not for inserting many independent flat rows of the same entity; use batch_insert for that.

batch_insert.title: Batch Insert
batch_insert.description: Insert many flat rows of the same entity in one operation. Each object is a plain map of scalar attribute values only — no relationships and no nested objects, which are ignored. If the rows have relationships or nested objects, use create instead (once per row).

batch_update.title: Batch Update
batch_update.description:
Update multiple entities matching an optional predicate in a single operation without loading objects into memory.
Values may be literal values or database expressions.
Returns the number of updated records.

batch_delete.title: Batch Delete
batch_delete.description:
Delete multiple entities matching a required predicate in a single operation.
Returns the number of deleted records.

persistent_history.title: Persistent History
persistent_history.description:
Fetch or purge the Core Data persistent history change log.
"operation":"purge" is destructive and permanently removes history transactions.
Both operations require exactly one scope parameter — "date", "transaction" or "token" — that marks the boundary: fetch returns history after it, purge removes history before it. When more than one is given, precedence is date > transaction > token.
"predicate" further filters the history in scope; it applies to both operations. It runs against "entity" — PersistentHistoryTransaction by default, or PersistentHistoryChange.
"resultType" applies to fetch only and is ignored for purge.
Only meaningful when persistent history tracking is enabled for the store.
